items.question: What is the status of first-trimester cardiac screening in low-risk pregnancies?
options: Shown to be effective, but neither routine nor mandatory
Mandatory at every nuchal translucency scan
Not possible before 18 weeks
Shown to be ineffective in low-risk populations
items.explanation: Early screening has been shown to be effective in low-risk populations but is neither routine nor mandatory; where possible it can be done at the nuchal translucency scan.

items.question: What are the minimum cardiac requirements at an early screen?
options: The heart is within the chest and the rhythm is regular
All five screening planes with colour Doppler
Both outflow tracts shown crossing
Pulsed-wave Doppler across all four valves
items.explanation: The minimum is seeing the heart within the chest and confirming a regular rhythm.

items.question: After what gestation is success in seeing cardiac structures significantly higher?
options: After 12 weeks and 3 days
After 10 weeks
After 11 weeks exactly
Gestation makes no difference within the 11 to 14 week window
items.explanation: Success in visualising cardiac structures is significantly higher after 12+3 weeks.

items.question: Which three components make up a detailed early cardiac screen?
options: Situs and axis; four-chamber view; three-vessel-and-trachea view
Four-chamber view; sagittal aortic arch; ductus venosus
Both outflow tracts; pulmonary veins; aortic isthmus
Upper abdomen; LVOT; RVOT
items.explanation: Situs and cardiac axis on grey-scale; four-chamber view on grey-scale and on colour and/or bidirectional power Doppler; three-vessel-and-trachea view on colour and/or bidirectional power Doppler.

items.question: At a detailed early screen, what should the three-vessel-and-trachea view show on colour or bidirectional power Doppler?
options: Aortic and ductal arches, both on the left
One arch on each side of the trachea
The pulmonary veins entering the left atrium
The moderator band
items.explanation: The early three-vessel-and-trachea view is used to show left-sided aortic and ductal arches.

items.question: What is the thermal index limit when Doppler is used at an early cardiac screen?
options: 1.0 or less
1.5 or less
3.0 or less
No limit applies to colour Doppler
items.explanation: The thermal index should be 1.0 or less, with exposure as short as possible.

items.question: How long should Doppler exposure usually last at an early cardiac screen?
options: As short as possible, usually no more than 5 to 10 minutes
As long as is needed to see every structure
At least 20 minutes for a complete study
Time is not relevant if the thermal index is below 2.0
items.explanation: Exposure should be as short as possible, usually no more than 5 to 10 minutes.

items.question: At 12 weeks the outflow tracts look possibly abnormal but the view is difficult. What next?
options: Refer for early fetal echocardiography: heart disease is suspected
Report a definite outflow-tract anomaly
Report the heart as normal, because early outflow views are unreliable
Wait until the third trimester
items.explanation: Early outflow-tract views are prone to false-positive and false-negative diagnosis; suspicion of congenital heart disease at the early scan should lead to referral for early fetal echocardiography.

items.question: Nuchal translucency was 3.8 mm at 12 weeks. A later measurement fell within the normal range. Is detailed cardiac evaluation still indicated?
options: Yes: 3.5 mm or more is an indication even if the measurement later becomes normal
No: the measurement has resolved
Only if another anomaly is found
Only if the family requests it
items.explanation: A nuchal translucency of 3.5 mm or more at 11 to 14 weeks is an indication for detailed cardiac evaluation even if it later falls within the normal range.

items.question: At the 11 to 14 week scan nuchal translucency is 3.2 mm. What does the guideline say about fetal echocardiography?
options: It may be considered
It is not relevant at this measurement
It is contraindicated before 20 weeks
It replaces the anomaly scan
items.explanation: With a nuchal translucency of 3.0 to 3.4 mm, fetal echocardiography may be considered; 3.5 mm or more is a listed indication.

items.question: Which transducers are recommended for early cardiac screening?
options: High-frequency transabdominal transducers; transvaginal may be used
Low-frequency transducers for better penetration
Transvaginal transducers only
Any transducer; frequency does not matter early in pregnancy
items.explanation: High-frequency transabdominal transducers are recommended and a transvaginal transducer may be used.
